reader.requirement: At --std 85 an argument-1 of RANDOM, when written, must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4) and is refused otherwise; its zero-or-positive half is a value constraint (undefined result when violated), and the value seeds a sequence that is the same for the same seed.

reader.notes: RANDOM's optional argument-1 is screened as an integer argument at --std 85 as at 2023, and a seed restarts a reproducible sequence. A negative seed is not refused, even as a literal; at 1985 it is a value constraint with an undefined result. Diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023:15.75.3.

refuter.evidence: fn_edge.cob at --std 85: COMPUTE F = FUNCTION RANDOM(N * (N + 1) / 2) refused, 'error COBOL1627: FUNCTION RANDOM argument-1 is an arithmetic expression whose term (N * (N + 1)) is an integer under the net factor 0.5 ...'; for N PIC 99 the seed is always a zero-or-positive integer, so §1989:A.2.35.3 AR1 with §1989:A.2.2 AR4 makes it legal. Same at --std 2023. Admitted: RANDOM(FUNCTION LENGTH(X)) = 0.33836984. Refused correctly: RANDOM(MEAN(1 2)), RANDOM(REM(7 2)) (numeric functions). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.35.3 AR1 'it must be zero or a positive integer'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4.
